newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Protest ends peacefully in Nigerian oil city.
newsitem.headline: Protest ends peacefully in Nigerian oil city.

text.p: Hundreds of protesters who filled the streets of Nigeria's tense southern oil city of Warri dispersed peacefully after a Tuesday demonstration against the government, witnesses said on Wednesday.
Staff at the independent Guardian newspaper said demonstrators took to the streets in the latest protest against the transfer of a local government headquarters.
"There was no trouble here in Warri, but we cannot be sure about what is going on outside the city," Peter Lele said by telephone.
"The navy says that everything is now calm in the riverine areas," he added.

Warri, the capital of one of Nigeria's main oil producing regions, is under a 7.p.m. to 6.a.m. curfew in the wake of disturbances caused by rivalry between three tribes -- the Ijaws, the Itsekiris and Urhobohs.
Last month oil output was hit hard when villagers occupied flow stations and took hostage 127 workers with Royal Dutch/ Shell who were freed after negotiations.
A Shell spokesman on Wednesday said that Tuesday's protest and tension in Warri had no effect on production which has now returned to normal.
